title: Network provenance and approval orchestration PRD (WIP)
content:
Summary:
This is a working PRD sketch to define how we capture network provenance and orchestrate approval gates for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). The goal is to make audit traces comprehensive and machine-actionable, while keeping the approval flow flexible for both self-service and operator-assisted handovers. This doc focuses on the event model (what we log), an approval orchestration state machine, operator UX constraints, and retention/archival proposals.

Why this matters:
- Customers running Private want clear evidence of who changed network attachments, who approved them, and what network policy versions were in effect.
- Existing change workflows are ad hoc; auditors ask for request/approval context tied to the exact runtime configuration used at the time of change.
- We must support both fast self-serve onboarding and SLA-backed operator interventions without losing auditable provenance.

Scope (in):
- API and console hooks to create/modify network handover requests (VPC endpoints, allowed-cidrs, peering, private-link-like connectors).
- An approval orchestration service with configurable gates (automated checks, customer approver, Redwood operator).
- Structured audit event schema for all relevant lifecycle steps (request, validate, approve, commit, rollback).
- Retention and export tools for audits (CSV/NDJSON export, S3 archival).

Scope (out):
- Low-level packet-level telemetry and flow logs (we will reference customer's own flow logs).
- Full policy governance engine (we'll integrate with customer's existing policy tools via validators).

Key personas:
- Platform Engineer (customer): wants an auditable, low-friction workflow to onboard model-serving endpoints into their VPC.
- Security Reviewer (customer): needs proof that approvals occurred and that rollback hooks exist.
- Redwood Operator: needs an operator console to expedite or intervene on escalations while preserving audit provenance.
- Compliance Auditor: needs exports with immutable IDs, timestamps, and object snapshots.

User stories (examples):
- As a platform engineer, I can create a network-change request with attachments (CIDR ranges, terraform plan id) and get either auto-approval or a customer approver step.
- As a security reviewer, I can see a snapshot of the accepted network config and the diff against the prior committed config.
- As a Redwood operator, I can place a hold on a request, add comments, and trigger a rollback if the customer requests emergency revoke.
- As an auditor, I can export all approvals for a date window with signed digests of the associated artifacts.

Functional requirements (high level):
- FR-01: Requests must accept attachments (manifest references), a human-readable justification, and an optional SLA tier selection.
- FR-02: Each request generates a globally unique immutable request_id (UUID v4) and an associated provenance token (signed by Redwood KMS).
- FR-03: The approval orchestrator must support configurable parallel gates: automated validators (policy checks), customer approver group, and Redwood ops approver group.
- FR-04: Approval actions (approve/reject/hold/comment) must be logged as structured audit events containing user id, actor role, timestamp, and approval metadata.
- FR-05: Committed network configuration snapshots must be stored as content-addressed blobs (sha256) and referenceable from audit events.
- FR-06: Exports must support filtered NDJSON and a signed manifest file that verifies the integrity of exported blobs.

Audit event schema (proposal):
- event_type: [string] (request_created, validator_passed, validator_failed, approver_action, commit, rollback, export_generated)
- timestamp: [ISO-8601 string]
- request_id: [UUID string]
- actor: [email user id or service principal]
- actor_role: [customer_platform, customer_security, redwood_operator, system_validator]
- action: [approve/reject/hold/auto-pass/auto-fail/commit/rollback/export]
- details_uri: [signed URL or internal blob id for the artifact: e.g., terraform-plan.json, adjacency-list.json]
- snapshot_sha256: [hex string] (if this event references committed snapshot)
- provenance_token: [base64-signed-token] (signed by Redwood KMS that binds request_id, snapshot_sha256, and time)

Implementation notes (internal):
- Use an append-only event store (Kafka topic + compacted backing in postgres) per-customer. Events are immutable; updates are modeled as new events.
- Store blobs in GCS with object versioning + customer-specific bucket prefixes to allow export and retention per contract.
- KMS signs provenance tokens; keep the signing key rotation policy documented in security playbook.
- Validators run as admission webhooks (can be remote calls to customer's policy engine). If validator times out, the gate can be configured to either fail closed or escalate to manual review.

Approval orchestration state machine (sketch):
- REQUEST_CREATED -> VALIDATION_RUNNING -> (VALIDATION_PASSED | VALIDATION_FAILED)
- VALIDATION_PASSED -> AWAITING_APPROVER -> (APPROVED -> COMMITTING -> COMMITTED) or (REJECTED -> CLOSED)
- AWAITING_APPROVER can have multiple parallel approver groups. A policy defines whether unanimous approval is required or majority.
- At any state redwood_operator can INTERVENE -> create INTERVENTION event -> either force COMMIT (with operator-justification) or HOLD.
- Rollback can be initiated from COMMITTED state and should produce ROLLBACK_STARTED -> ROLLBACK_COMPLETED events. Rollback must reference the prior snapshot sha.

Operator UX considerations:
- Console should show: request timeline (events), diff viewer, attached artifacts (downloadable), provenance token, and one-click export for compliance.
- Temporarily sensitive fields (customer IP ranges) should be masked in operator view unless operator role has explicit authorization. Masking must be recorded in audit events (MASK_VIEW event).
- Bulk action support for operators to close multiple stale requests. Bulk actions must emit a single bulk_event containing list of request_ids and individual sub-events for each.

Retention & archival policy (proposal):
- Default retention: 365 days for events and 365 days for blobs for self-serve customers.
- Enterprise customers can request longer retention via contract (e.g., 7 years) with premium archival storage and legal-hold options.
- Exports: provide a signed tarball with NDJSON events + blob directory + manifest.sig. Manifest contains hashes and a KMS signature.

Security and compliance notes:
- Strong authentication required: SSO (OIDC) for customer actors; operator actions require MFA enforced.
- Provenance tokens must include nonce and timestamp to prevent replay. Tokens are short-lived for live validation but long-lived signatures (with key rotation) exist for archival verification.
- Ensure separation of duties: operator role cannot both approve and perform commit for the same request without additional justification and logging.

Performance and scale considerations:
- Typical burst pattern during onboarding windows (hours 0-4 of a deployment) — small requests but frequent. Event store must handle spikes (design target: 200 reqs/min per customer peak).
- Snapshot storage cost: we will deduplicate snapshots by content SHA and store references to avoid duplicating identical blobs.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment): instrument event schema and provenance token for a single pilot customer; manual enforcement of approval gates. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1 (self-serve): implement orchestrator, basic console UI, exports, and default retention. Invite 5 customers. (4 sprints)
- Phase 2 (enterprise): add operator roles, masking controls, contract extensions for retention, and complex validator integrations (SaaS policy engines). (3 sprints)

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Q1: Should provenance token be a structured JWS with embedded snapshot hash, or a separate signed manifest file? Pros/cons: JWS makes single-token verification easier; manifest better for large sets.
- Q2: What is the canonical attachment format for network snapshots? Terraform plan JSON? YAML adjacency? Need to standardize for diffs.
- Q3: Default gate policy for validator timeouts: fail-closed or escalate to manual review?

Action items / next steps:
- [Sofia] Draft schema pull request and reference implementation for token signing (GH issue).
- [Emil] Prototype console timeline UI wireframe and a masked-view demo.
- [Rhea] Reach out to pilot customer (Acme Health) to validate artifact formats and retention requirements.
- [Marcus] Build a quick NDJSON export utility and manifest signer CLI.

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally lightweight and iterative. Primary goals are to: (1) make audit traces machine-friendly, (2) preserve exact config snapshots referenced by approvals, and (3) give operators safe, auditable levers to assist customers. Please add comments inline in Confluence link or drop notes in #private-deployments slack thread.

-- end of sketch --
